The contrast between Spain's winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.

more.summary: Sleep is fundamental to well-being. more.title: Heavy hydrogen in 3I/ATLAS's methane points to a frigid birthplace
more.summary: The interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS carries a chemical clue to conditions in the planetary system of its origin, locked away long before it reached our sun. Its methane signature is unusually rich in heavy hydrogen, suggesting that the comet's frozen ingredients took shape in an intensely cold environment around another star—or in the cloud that preceded it.

more.title: 2,700-year-old mummy head yields first molecular evidence linking aloe to Egyptian embalming
more.summary: What materials did ancient Egyptians use to preserve the dead, and how can their composition still be investigated thousands of years later? An interdisciplinary team at Marburg University has combined modern natural product analysis with Egyptology and the history of pharmacy to investigate these questions.

more.title: Scientists shrink Archimedes’ screw to the size of a single molecule
more.summary: Scientists have built a groundbreaking molecular motor that spins in either direction using electricity, inspired by a machine invented more than 2,000 years ago. Even more remarkably, its rotation can boost electrical conductivity by up to 100 times, potentially transforming the future of molecular electronics.

more.title: Scientists use sound waves to deliver a new attack on deadly brain cancer
more.summary: Scientists at the University of Virginia have developed a promising new strategy to fight glioblastoma, one of the deadliest and most difficult-to-treat forms of brain cancer. Their experimental approach combines focused ultrasound, tiny nanoparticles, and genetic molecules called microRNAs to attack multiple cancer-driving genes simultaneously.
